title: One Cave Hid 50,000 Manuscripts for 900 Years | Silk Road EP1 | China Travel Expert
description:
One desert cave hid about 50,000 manuscripts for nearly 900 years. This is the Mogao Caves, on China's old Silk Road.

Near the oasis town of Dunhuang in Gansu, around 500 decorated caves are cut into a single cliff — the "Thousand Buddha Grottoes," carved over a thousand years of Silk Road traffic. In 1900 a Daoist caretaker, Wang Yuanlu, stumbled onto a small sealed chamber (Cave 17, the "Library Cave"). Inside were tens of thousands of scrolls, booklets and silk paintings in 17 languages — a find scholars have compared to opening Tutankhamun's tomb.

🧭 Expert Tip: Book Mogao tickets in advance — the Dunhuang Academy caps and times daily visitors to protect the murals, and peak-season slots sell out.
